name: HR and recruitment agencies

problems.words: Clients take weeks to give interview feedback and candidates go elsewhere
quick_ideas: Agree a feedback date with the client each time you send a shortlist, so there is something to hold them to
List every shortlist currently waiting on feedback, so you know which clients to chase today.

workzap_build.text: a feedback chaser that reminds the client when a shortlist has had no response after a set number of days, with a daily list of stalled shortlists for the account manager.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many open roles are you working on right now?
problems.free_stops: chaser timings and escalation per client are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each client's last three feedback delays beside the role, so you see which accounts are losing candidates most often.
Give one recruiter the job of chasing every waiting shortlist at one set time, so no client silence sits untouched for days.

problems.words: Candidates accept and then don't show up on day one
quick_ideas: Call each candidate due to join in the next fortnight once, so you hear about doubts before day one
Keep one backup candidate warm for each of those roles, so a drop-out doesn't reset the search.

workzap_build.text: a candidate pipeline per job order through offered, confirmed, joined and in guarantee, with check-in tasks created before the joining date.

problems.ask_first: Do the no-shows come mostly from one type of role, or from one client?
problems.free_stops: the check-in points and backup rules are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many accepted candidates went silent before joining this month, so you see where day one risk is highest.
Give one recruiter the handover call for every confirmed starter, so doubts are heard before the joining date.

problems.words: The same candidate is in our system three times with different CVs
quick_ideas: Clean one active role's candidate list of duplicates, so you see how big the problem is
Agree that everyone searches before adding a candidate, so new duplicates slow down.

workzap_build.text: duplicate detection when a candidate is added, with the source and the recruiter who added them recorded at the same moment.

problems.ask_first: Do the duplicates come from candidates applying again, or from different recruiters adding them?
problems.free_stops: how matches are detected and how credit is recorded is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare candidate records added this week for matching phone endings or email patterns, so you see where duplicate entry starts.
Give one person the job of checking new active records before filing, so duplicate profiles stop spreading across live roles.

problems.words: Recruiters keep their best candidates in their own phones, and the pipeline leaves with them
quick_ideas: Ask each recruiter to move their active candidates into the shared list, with the candidates' permission, so the agency holds the pipeline
Review that list with the team once, so gaps show.

workzap_build.text: one shared pipeline per job order owned by the agency, so every candidate, stage and note stays when a recruiter leaves.

problems.ask_first: Is it mostly the senior recruiters who keep candidates on their phones, or everyone?
problems.free_stops: access rights and how the pipeline is structured are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count active roles where candidate contact sits only with one recruiter, so you see how exposed the pipeline is.
Give each live role one shared notebook page for candidate stage notes, so handovers still happen when staff leave.

problems.words: Recruiters argue over who sourced the placed candidate
quick_ideas: Write down one clear rule for who gets credit, so arguments have something to refer to
Note the source recruiter on every current placement, so this month's commission is settled.

workzap_build.text: source and recruiter credit recorded the moment a candidate enters, with a commission view each recruiter can see.

problems.ask_first: Do the arguments start when a candidate was sourced by one recruiter and closed by another?
problems.free_stops: the credit rules and commission view are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every current placement with who opened the client and who introduced the candidate, so the disputed points are visible early.
Give one manager the job of marking credit on each live placement list, so arguments stop reopening old deals.

problems.words: I can't see how many CVs each recruiter sent this week
quick_ideas: Ask each recruiter for one weekly count of CVs sourced, shortlisted and interviews arranged, so you get a first picture
Look at those counts side by side once, so you see where help is needed.

workzap_build.text: a recruiter activity board updated every day from the pipeline, showing CVs, shortlists, interviews and placements per person.

problems.ask_first: Which count do you most want to see weekly, CVs sent, interviews arranged or placements made?
problems.free_stops: which activities to measure and how is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count each recruiter's shortlisted candidates and interviews arranged this week, so you can compare output across the same period.
Give one team lead one notebook page for weekly recruiter totals, so performance is reviewed from one place.

problems.words: Clients delay paying placement fees until after probation
quick_ideas: List every placement with its joining date and invoice status, so missing invoices show
Check each client's fee terms once, so you know when payment is actually due.

workzap_build.text: fee invoicing triggered by the joining date, with receivables ageing, guarantee end dates and reminders sent on schedule.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few large clients who hold fees back, or most clients?
problems.free_stops: the invoicing triggers and reminder sequence are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count placements already working where no invoice has been sent, so missed billing gets spotted before payment is delayed further.
Give one person the weekly handover list of joined candidates awaiting invoices, so fee chasing starts from the right accounts.

problems.words: Contract staff timesheets come in wrong and we pay the wrong amount
quick_ideas: Ask each client supervisor to confirm this week's hours in writing, so payroll uses agreed figures
Note last month's corrections once, so you see which sites cause errors.

workzap_build.text: timesheets captured on phone, approved by the client supervisor, and fed into both payroll and client billing.

problems.ask_first: Do the wrong timesheets come from a few client sites, or from many?
problems.free_stops: the approval flow and how it links to payroll are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which client sites sent corrected hours most often this month, so you see where wrong timesheets keep starting.
Give one staff member the single list of pending hour confirmations, so payroll stops using scattered messages and guesses.

problems.words: Job board subscriptions cost a lot and we don't know which one works
quick_ideas: Note the source of each placement from the last few months, so you get a first view of which boards deliver
Ask new applicants where they saw the role, so the gap fills from today.

workzap_build.text: separate application links per job board and channel, so every placement shows where it came from.

problems.ask_first: How many job boards do you pay for, and do applicants usually say which one they used?
problems.free_stops: how sources are tagged and reported is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count recent placements by lead source written on existing role notes, so you see which channels actually convert to hires.
Give one recruiter the job of writing one source label on every new applicant note, so future comparisons come from one routine.

problems.words: Our WhatsApp is flooded with candidates asking for updates
quick_ideas: Send one update to every candidate on active roles, so the backlog of questions drops
Agree fixed hours for answering status queries, so recruiters get time back.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp updates sent to candidates, with their permission, each time they move to a new stage.

problems.ask_first: Do most candidates ask about interview dates, or about the result after an interview?
problems.free_stops: which stages trigger an update is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count update messages by role for one busy day, so you see which vacancies create most chasing.
Give one recruiter the update queue at a fixed time daily, so candidate replies stop interrupting everyone else.

never_say: Any visa, work permit, immigration or labour-law advice, or salary benchmarking as advice.
Anything involving fake experience letters, forged degrees or false references.
Help with filtering candidates by religion, nationality or gender where unlawful, or charging candidates unlawful fees.
That candidates will always join or that time-to-fill will drop by any amount.
Requests for candidate CVs, names, numbers, ID or salary details.

sample_reply.person: Clients feedback dene mein hafte laga dete hain aur candidates nikal jate hain. Koi hal batayein.
sample_reply.pi:
Haan, is ko behtar kiya ja sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, har shortlist ke saath client se feedback ki ek tareekh tay karein, taake follow up ka buniyaad ho.
Doosra, aaj ek dafa woh sab shortlists likh lein jin ka feedback ruka hua hai, taake pata ho ke kis client ko pehle yaad dilana hai.
Workzap is tarah ka intezam kar sakta hai: feedback ruke to client ko khud reminder, aur candidates ko har stage pe unki ijazat se update.
